terms.register: vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Plaut., Ter.; also Verg. (E. 1.15)
evidence: Ter. Haut. 934b: Āh, nescīs quam doleam.
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: of pain or grief; of entreaty to avert something (āh, nōlī, “ah, don’t!”); of indignation (āh, rogitās?); of admonition (āh, dēsine); of consolation.
Lewis & Short: astonishment, joy, anger. Augustine (In Joh. 51): cum dolentēs dīcimus heu! vel cum dēlectāmur vah dīcimus. For its contemptuous use see bah!.

phrases.english: Ah, you don’t know how it hurts.
Ah, absolutely not; I won’t do it.

sources: Lewis & Short: ah (ā) · Lewis & Short: vah
